title: Shrinking a finite type model to the etale complement from its completed Jacobian
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, and $C$ a finite type commutative $A$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Suppose its $I$-adic completion $\widehat C_I$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] admits an $A$-algebra presentation $\widehat C_I\cong P/J$, where $P=\widehat{A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]}_I$ for finite $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and $J\subseteq P$ is an ideal. Suppose some $I^c$, $c\geq0$, annihilates both kernel and cokernel of $J/J^2\to(P/J)^{\oplus r}$, $f\mapsto(\partial f/\partial x_i)_i$, with continuous derivatives. Then there exists $g\in1+IC$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-etale-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), part (2), with Tag 0AJU (lemma-equivalent-with-artin), condition (3), and Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion).

proof.text: Choose a finite polynomial presentation $\alpha:Q=A[y_1,\ldots,y_s]\twoheadrightarrow C$ with kernel $K$, using the finite type hypothesis. Both $Q$ and $C$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Thus choose finite ideal generators $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ of $K$. Their classes generate $K/K^2$ over $C$: coefficients in $Q$ can be reduced modulo $K$. Define $d_\alpha:K/K^2\to C^{\oplus s}$ by the polynomial derivatives, and set $M_1=\ker d_\alpha$, $M_0=\operatorname{coker}d_\alpha$. The submodule theorem [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented] makes $M_1$ finite; $M_0$ is generated by the images of the $s$ standard basis vectors. Consequently $H=M_1\oplus M_0$ is a finite $C$-module.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), proof, finiteness of the ordinary naive cotangent homology.

proof.text: Compose the given presentation isomorphism with $P\twoheadrightarrow P/J$ to get a surjection $P\to\widehat C_I$ with kernel $J$. Apply [lem-per-completed-jacobian-homology-comparison] to this presentation and $\alpha$. It identifies $\widehat M_1$ with the given Jacobian kernel and $\widehat M_0$ with its cokernel. Hence $I^c$ annihilates both completions. Completion commutes with the displayed finite direct sum by taking the two coordinates of each compatible sequence, so $(IC)^c\widehat H=0$.

source.place: Tags 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), 0GAE (lemma-NL-up-to-homotopy), and the hypothesis in the proof of 0ALQ.

proof.text: Put $L=IC$ and $N=L^cH\subseteq H$. It is finite by [lem-trf-noetherian-submodule-finitely-presented]. Choose finite generators $b_1,\ldots,b_u$ of $L^c$; the map $H^{\oplus u}\twoheadrightarrow N$, $(h_j)\mapsto\sum_jb_jh_j$, is surjective. All its kernel and image modules are finite, so [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] makes $\widehat H^{\oplus u}\to\widehat N$ surjective and $\widehat N\to\widehat H$ injective. Their composite is zero: each $b_j$ kills $\widehat H$ by Step 2. Surjectivity followed by injectivity therefore implies $\widehat N=0$. Apply the same exact-completion statement to $0\to LN\to N\to N/LN\to0$. It gives $\widehat{N/LN}=0$. Since $L$ kills $N/LN$, every positive-level quotient in this last completion equals $N/LN$, with identity transition maps. Thus $N/LN=0$, equivalently $LN=N$.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), proof of (2), Nakayama passage expanded; exact completion is Algebra Tag 00MB (lemma-completion-flat).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-one-plus-ideal-annihilator] with ring $C$, ideal $L$ and finite module $N$. It supplies $g\in C$ with $g-1\in L=IC$ and $gN=0$. In particular $gL^cM_i=0$ for $i=0,1$. This is one common $g$ for both homology modules, as required.

source.place: Algebra Tag 00DV (lemma-NAK), item (1); applied as in Restricted Power Series Tag 0ALQ.

proof.text: Fix $a\in I$, write $\bar a$ for its image in $C$, and put $v=g\bar a$. In $C_v$ both $g$ and $\bar a$ are units (their inverses are $\bar a/v$ and $g/v$). Since $\bar a^c\in L^c$, Step 4 says that the unit $g\bar a^c$ annihilates $(M_i)_v$. Therefore $(M_1)_v=(M_0)_v=0$. Exactness of module localization [lem-sc-p1-localization-short-exact], applied to the kernel, image and cokernel sequences of $d_\alpha$, shows that $d_\alpha\otimes_CC_v$ has zero kernel and cokernel.

source.place: Tag 0ALQ (lemma-rig-etale), proof of (2), vanishing off V(I); localization exactness is Algebra Tag 00CS (proposition-localization-exact).

proof.text: Lift $v$ to $\widetilde v\in Q$ and use the polynomial presentation $\alpha_v:Q[z]\twoheadrightarrow C_v$, $z\mapsto v^{-1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-naive-cotangent], its kernel is $(K,\widetilde v z-1)$ and its two-term conormal complex is the direct sum of the localized complex of $\alpha$ and the acyclic complex $C_v\xrightarrow{v}C_v$. The identification of polynomial differentials with coordinate derivatives is [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis]. Thus its two homology modules vanish by Step 5. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-nl-presentations-homotopy-equivalent] to $\alpha_v$ and the canonical polynomial presentation of $C_v$ from [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map]; its homotopy identities give inverse maps on kernels and cokernels. By [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-kahler-basis-any-variables], $C_v\otimes\Omega_{A[C_v]/A}$ is free on the $1\otimes\mathrm d[s]$ with $1\otimes\mathrm dp\mapsto\sum_s\gamma(\partial p/\partial[s])\,\mathrm d[s]$, so the canonical kernel is $H_1(L_{C_v/A})=\ker\delta=0$. The quotient conormal sequence [lem-weil-pbc-jacobi-zariski-differential-maps] identifies the cokernel with $\Omega_{C_v/A}$, so this module also vanishes. Finally, $C_v=A[y_1,\ldots,y_s,z]/(k_1,\ldots,k_t,\widetilde v z-1)$ is finitely presented, with no regular-sequence assumption on the $k_j$.

The finite presentation and the two vanishings in Step 6 give that $\operatorname{Spec}C_{g\bar a}\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-map-iff-etale-affine]. Inside $\operatorname{Spec}C_g$, the inverse image of $\operatorname{Spec}A\setminus V(I)$ is the union, over $a\in I$, of the affine opens $D(\bar a)=\operatorname{Spec}C_{g\bar a}$. Indeed a prime of $C_g$ lies over that complement exactly when its contraction to $A$ omits some $a\in I$. The affine-cover formulation of [def-weil-etale-morphism] therefore says precisely that $\operatorname{Spec}C_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale over this complement. Step 4 gives $g\in1+IC$, completing the assertion.
